title: Entity Relationship Diagrams for Data Structures

text.insert: This spec proposes entity relationship diagrams (ERDs) as a component for system design pages, specs, and plans. An ERD draws each record as a box of fields and each reference as a line between two fields, with cardinality at both ends. text.insert: No format keeps a full layout in its text. Tools that persist positions keep them in app state, as dbdiagram and Azimutt do.
Five patterns recur across ERD tools and apply directly to docs pages.
dbdiagram and Liam ERD switch between table names, keys only, and all fields. In names-only mode an edge attaches to the table header.
ChartDB and Azimutt collapse long tables but keep the primary key and every row that an edge attaches to.
Liam dims everything except the active table, its neighbors, and their edges.

Published evidence on agent-authored diagrams favors typed edits over regenerated text. Most of it comes from practitioner reports, not controlled studies.
Practitioner reports describe syntax errors and unstable node ids when models write Mermaid or PlantUML directly.
Tools that edit one diagram over many turns, such as Zindex and the Straightedge MCP server, keep stable ids and apply typed operations.

Each question carries a recommended default, so Phase 1 can start before it is answered.
Does line style mean declared versus logical, or identifying versus non-identifying?
Recommended default is declared versus logical. On the trace-store board, 8 of 14 links are logical and none is identifying.
Recommended default is elkjs, lazy-loaded. Dagre has no ports, and the canvas router routes lines but places nothing.
May docs-viewer import a canvas routing leaf?
Recommended default is no for Phase 1, because docs-viewer has no canvas dependency today.
The block routes its own row-attached lines, and Phase 4 revisits sharing the canvas router.
Does an ERD replace linkage tables?
Recommended default is no. The diagram replaces the columns that say which field points where, and a table keeps facts such as when a field is stamped.
